tb-404-1.question:
(For Q1–2.) An electrical appliance is faulty, and the live wire accidentally touches the metal case (Fig a).

If no earth wire is installed, which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) The fuse will blow.

(2) The metal case will remain live.

(3) The appliance will not work.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-404-1.reasoning:
As the metal case is not earthed, current flows from the live wire to the neutral wire through the load (or the opposite direction). The size of the current in the live wire is equal to the operating current, so the fuse will not blow.

∴ (1) and (3) are incorrect.

The metal case is connected to the live wire.

∴ (2) is correct.

tb-404-2.question:
(For Q1–2.) An electrical appliance is faulty, and the live wire accidentally touches the metal case (Fig a).

If an earth wire is installed, which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) The fuse will blow.

(2) The metal case will remain live.

(3) The appliance will not work.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-404-2.reasoning:
A large current will flow through the live wire and the earth wire due to the short circuit. So, the fuse will blow.

∴ (1) and (3) are correct.

The metal case is not live after the fuse blows.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

tb-404-3.question:
A kettle is plugged into a wall socket and works normally. Which of the following statements is/ are correct?

(1) The current flows through the kettle in alternate directions.

(2) The live, neutral and earth wires form a closed circuit for current to flow through.

(3) The current in the live wire is as large as that in the neutral wire.

A (1) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-404-3.reasoning:
A wall socket provides a.c.

∴ (1) is correct.

No current flow through the earth wire when the appliance is working normally.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

The current entering the appliance is the same as the current leaving the appliance.

∴ (3) is correct.

B The power consumption of X is double the power consumption of Y.

Consider the ratings of X.

R =V2P=110225= 484 Ω

Consider the ratings of Y.

R =110250= 242 Ω

Total power consumption

=V2R

=2202484+242

= 66.7 W

tb-404-6.question:
Which of the following is/are the function(s) of the earth wire?

(1) It prevents the appliance from overheating.

(2) It prevents users from getting an electric shock.

(3) It keeps the potential of the neutral wire at 0 V.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-404-6.reasoning:
The earth wire keeps the potential of the metal body of appliance at 0 V.

∴ (2) is correct.

tb-404-7.question:
Which of the following is/are the advantage(s) of using several parallel branch circuits over one big circuit to supply electricity to all appliances in a house?

(1) Cheaper cables can be used in the branches.

(2) Appliances and circuits can be protected by suitable circuit breakers.

(3) A fault usually affects one branch but not the whole house.

A (1) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-404-7.reasoning:
Thinner and cheaper cables can be used in the branches as the current is smaller in each branch circuit.

∴ (1) is correct.

Each branch is fitted with a circuit breaker of suitable value.

∴ (2) is correct.

The branches are connected in parallel. Other branches are unaffected when a fault develops in a branch.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-404-8.question:
A bulb rated ‘220 V, 60 W’ is connected to a 220-V mains supply. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) Its highest instantaneous power is 60 W.

(2) Its average power is 60 W.

(3) It has the same output power if it is connected to a 220-V d.c. power supply.

A (1) only

B (2) only

C (1) and (3) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-404-8.reasoning:
The rated power is the average power of the bulb when working at the rated voltage.

∴ (2) is correct. (1) is incorrect.

The r.m.s. voltage of the mains supply is 220 V. It delivers the same power as a 220-V d.c. power supply.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-404-11.question:
Figure c shows the circuit of an electric heater.

The fuse blows when the heater is switched on. Which of the following could be the cause?

(1) The insulation at point X is worn out such that the wire touches the metal case.

(2) The insulation at point Y is worn out such that the wire touches the metal case.

(3) The heating element is broken.

A (1) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-404-11.reasoning:
If the insulation at X is worn out, a large current will flow through the live wire and the earth wire due to the short circuit. So, the fuse will blow.

∴ (1) is correct.

If the insulation at Y is worn out, current flows from the live wire to the neutral and earth wires through the heating element (or the opposite direction). The size of the current in the live wire is equal to the operating current, so the fuse will not blow.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

If the heating element is broken, the circuit is not complete and no current flows through the live wire, so the fuse will not blow.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-404-12.question:
An electric stewing pot has three heating elements, each of resistance 100 Ω (Fig d).

Which of the following connections can boil water the fastest?
tb-404-12.reasoning: By P = V2R, to boil water the fastest, P should be maximized and hence R should be minimized. To do so, the heating elements should be connected in parallel.

tb-404-17.question:
A 10-A fuse is at 25 °C initially. The fuse wire melts after a current of 20 A flows through it for time T. Assume that the resistance of the wire remains at 0.008 Ω.

(a) Explain the function of a fuse. (2 marks)

(b) Estimate the power dissipated by the fuse wire when the 20-A current is flowing through it. (2 marks)

(d) State an assumption that you made in (c). Explain how this assumption affects the answer in (c). (3 marks)
tb-404-17.answer:
(a) When an excess current flows through the live wire, the fuse will blow and the circuit becomes open. 1A

This prevents the appliance from overheating and catching fire. 1A

(b) P = I 2R

= (20)2(0.008) 1M

= 3.2 W 1A

(c) E = Pt = CΔT

(3.2)T = (0.03)(700 – 25) 1M + 1M

T = 6.33 s 1A

(d) The heat loss is assumed to be negligible. 1A

However, the heat loss becomes more significant as the temperature of the fuse wire increases. 1A

The actual time taken for the fuse wire to melt is longer than 6.33 s. 1A

tb-404-18.question:
Figure g shows a part of a household electrical wiring plan. At the consumer unit, the wires branch out into several parallel circuits. The branch leading to a ring main is fitted with a 30-A circuit breaker.

(a) Should the current rating of wire X be larger or smaller than 30 A? Explain. (2 marks)

(b) Why is the air conditioner not connected to the ring main? (2 marks)

(c) Five sockets, each protected by a 13-A fuse, are connected to the ring main.

(i) State a difference between a circuit breaker and a fuse. (1 mark)

(ii) Are the sockets connected in parallel or in series? Suggest two advantages of this kind of connection. (3 marks)

(iii) Jimmy says that the circuit breaker will certainly be triggered because the total current drawn by the sockets is greater than 30 A. Comment on this statement. (2 marks)

(iv) Karen says that the circuit breaker will never be triggered because its rating is larger than the rating of the fuses protecting the sockets. Comment on this statement. (2 marks)
tb-404-18.answer:
(a) A 30-A fuse is installed in wire X.

The rating of wire X should be larger than 30 A 1A

so that it can carry a maximum current of at least 30 A. 1A

(b) The air conditioner draws a large current. 1A

It should be connected to a separated circuit parallel to the ring main to avoid overloading. 1A

(c) (i) A circuit breaker can be reset by simply pushing the switch. A blown fuse has to be replaced by a new one. 1A

(ii) Parallel. 1A

Appliances connected to different sockets work independently. 1A

All sockets work at the mains voltage. 1A

(iii) Incorrect. 1A

The actual current drawn from each socket is less than 13 A. The circuit breaker will not be trigger as long as the total current is less than 30 A.
1A

(iv) Incorrect. 1A

The maximum total current allowed by all five sockets is 65 A (5 x 13 A) and is larger than the rating of the circuit breaker. 1A

tb-404-22.question:
Immersion heater X is connected to the 220-V mains and is used to boil 2 kg of water at 25 °C. Only 85% of the energy input to X becomes the internal energy of the water. The specific heat capacity of water is 4200 J kg–1 °C–1.

(a) Find the cost of boiling the water. (3 marks)

(b) Immersion heater Y is also connected to the mains and is used to boil 2 kg of water at 25 °C. Like X, only 85% of the energy input to Y becomes the internal energy of the water. The power of Y is lower than that of X. Compare the cost of boiling the water using X and Y. Explain. (2 marks)

(c) X and Y are now connected in series to the mains.

(i) Which heater has a higher power consumption? (3 marks)

(ii) A student suggests that the time needed to boil the water using this set-up will be shorter than using either heater alone. Comment on this idea. (3 marks)
tb-404-22.answer:
(a) Electrical energy needed to boil the water

= mcΔT ÷ 85%

= (2)(4200)(100 – 25) ÷ 85% 1M

= 7.412 × 105 J

=7.412×1051000×3600kW h

= 0.2059 kW h 1M

Cost of electricity

= $1.1 × E

= $1.1 × 0.2059

= $0.226 1A

(b) The same amount of electrical energy is needed to boil the water as they have the same efficiency. 1A

Therefore, the cost of electricity is the same. 1A

(c) (i) By P =V2R, when connected to the mains, the power of Y is lower than the power of X, so the resistance of Y is higher than the resistance of X. 1A

The same current flows through X and Y when they are connected in series. By P = I 2R, 1A

Y has a higher power consumption. 1A

(ii) Incorrect. 1A

Connecting the heaters in series has a higher equivalent resistance than either one of them. 1A

By P =V2R, the total power dissipated by the heaters connected in series is lower than using either heater alone. 1A

Therefore, it takes a long time to boil the water.
